an implement whose revolving concave discs cut and invert the soil
the pull required for each unit width of an implement
items.s: harrow: an implement with many tines or discs used to break clods and level a seedbed. The other options describe unit draft, clod, disc plough.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines volumetric efficiency.
o: the share of the heat energy in the fuel that is turned into useful work at the shaft
the ratio of the volume of air actually drawn in to the swept volume of the cylinders
the mass of air supplied for each unit mass of fuel burned
the mass of fuel burned for each unit of work delivered at the shaft
items.s: volumetric efficiency: the ratio of the volume of air actually drawn in to the swept volume of the cylinders. The other options describe thermal efficiency, air fuel ratio, specific fuel consumption.

items.q: rotavator may be defined as
o: an implement whose revolving concave discs cut and invert the soil
a lump of soil left unbroken after a tillage operation
an implement that cuts, lifts and turns a furrow slice over
a machine whose powered blades chop and mix the soil in a single pass
items.s: rotavator: a machine whose powered blades chop and mix the soil in a single pass. The other options describe mouldboard plough, clod, disc plough.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines mouldboard plough.
o: the horizontal force needed to pull an implement through the soil
a lump of soil left unbroken after a tillage operation
an implement that cuts, lifts and turns a furrow slice over
the pull required for each unit width of an implement
items.s: mouldboard plough: an implement that cuts, lifts and turns a furrow slice over. The other options describe unit draft, draft, clod.

items.q: swept volume may be defined as
o: the volume displaced by the piston as it travels from the top to the bottom of its stroke
a cycle in which every turn of the crankshaft produces one power stroke
the sequence of intake, compression, power and exhaust strokes completed in two turns of the crankshaft
the space left above the piston when it stands at the top of its travel
items.s: swept volume: the volume displaced by the piston as it travels from the top to the bottom of its stroke. The other options describe two stroke cycle, four stroke cycle, clearance volume.

items.q: Which of the following best describes germination percentage?
o: the number of plants standing on a unit area of land
the part of a seeder that measures out seed at a steady rate
the proportion of seeds that produce normal seedlings under test conditions
the mass of one thousand seeds of a crop, used to turn seed numbers into mass
items.s: germination percentage: the proportion of seeds that produce normal seedlings under test conditions. The other options describe metering mechanism, thousand grain weight, plant population.

items.q: Which of the following best describes planter?
o: the mass or number of seeds sown on a unit area of land
a machine that places individual seeds or vegetative material at a set spacing
the part of a seeder that measures out seed at a steady rate
the number of plants standing on a unit area of land
items.s: planter: a machine that places individual seeds or vegetative material at a set spacing. The other options describe seed rate, plant population, metering mechanism.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines custom hire?
o: an expense that is incurred whether the machine works or not
the letting out of a machine and its operator to another farmer for a fee
the number of years a machine is expected to serve before replacement
an expense that rises with the amount of work the machine does
items.s: custom hire: the letting out of a machine and its operator to another farmer for a fee. The other options describe useful life, fixed cost, variable cost.

items.q: An implement of width 3 m working at a depth of 0.18 m requires a draft of 7500 N. Calculate the specific draft in kPa.
items.s: Area of soil cut = 3 x 0.18 = 0.54 m2, so specific draft = 7500/0.54 = 13889 Pa = 13.89 kPa.

items.q: A seed rate gives a population of 150000 plants per hectare and the thousand grain weight of the seed is 30 g. Calculate the mass of seed required per hectare in kg.
items.s: Seed mass = population x thousand grain weight/1000000 = 150000 x 30/1000000 = 4.5 kg per hectare.

items.q: A machine costs 4000000 naira, will be worth 600000 naira at the end of its life, and the rate of interest on capital is 14 percent. Calculate the average annual interest charge in naira.
items.s: Average investment = (4000000 + 600000)/2 = 2300000, so interest = 2300000 x 14/100 = 322000 naira per year.

items.q: A pump delivers 12 litres per second against a total head of 30 m with an efficiency of 75 percent. Calculate the power required to drive it in kW.
items.s: Power = 9.81 x discharge x head/(1000 x efficiency) = 9.81 x 12 x 30/(1000 x 0.75) = 4.71 kW.

items.q: An engine has a compression ratio of 16 and a swept volume of 900 cm3. Calculate its clearance volume in cm3.
items.s: Clearance volume = swept volume/(compression ratio - 1) = 900/15 = 60 cm3.

items.q: A 3 cylinder four stroke engine has a bore of 105 mm and a stroke of 110 mm. Calculate its total piston displacement in litres.
items.s: One cylinder displaces 952.5 cm3, so 3 cylinders displace 3 x 952.5 = 2858 cm3 = 2.86 litres.

items.q: A tractor engine runs at 2200 revolutions per minute and has a stroke of 110 mm. Calculate the mean piston speed in m/s.
items.s: Mean piston speed = 2 x stroke x speed/60 = 2 x 0.11 x 2200/60 = 8.07 m/s.

items.q: An engine uses 6 kg of fuel per hour, the fuel having a calorific value of 45 MJ/kg, and delivers 52 kW at the shaft. Calculate its brake thermal efficiency in percent.
items.s: Fuel power = 6 x 45/3.6 = 75 kW. Thermal efficiency = 52/75 x 100 = 69.3 percent.

items.q: A tractor engine consumes 15 kg of diesel per hour while delivering 45 kW at the shaft. Calculate the specific fuel consumption in kg/kWh.
items.s: Specific fuel consumption = fuel used per hour/power = 15/45 = 0.333 kg/kWh.

items.q: An engine takes in 780 kg of air per hour and burns 55 kg of fuel in the same period. Calculate the air fuel ratio.
items.s: Air fuel ratio = mass of air/mass of fuel = 780/55 = 14.2.

items.q: A tractor pulls an implement with a draft of 7.5 kN at a forward speed of 6 km/h. Calculate the drawbar power in kW.
items.s: Drawbar power = draft x speed/3.6 = 7.5 x 6/3.6 = 12.5 kW.

items.q: A tractor wheel would cover 300 m in a given time if it rolled without slipping but it actually covers 270 m. Calculate the wheel slip in percent.
items.s: Slip = (theoretical distance - actual distance)/theoretical distance x 100 = (300 - 270)/300 x 100 = 10 percent.

items.q: A trailer of weight 36 kN runs on a soil whose coefficient of rolling resistance is 0.08. Calculate the rolling resistance in kN.
items.s: Rolling resistance = coefficient x weight = 0.08 x 36 = 2.88 kN.

items.q: The torque at the axle of a tractor wheel is 3600 N m and the rolling radius of the wheel is 0.6 m. Calculate the tractive force at the rim in N.
items.s: Tractive force = torque/radius = 3600/0.6 = 6000 N.

items.q: A drawbar pull of 7.5 kN must be developed on a soil where the coefficient of traction is 0.6. Calculate the vertical load needed on the driving wheels in kN.
items.s: Vertical load = pull/coefficient of traction = 7.5/0.6 = 12.5 kN.

items.q: An engine turning at 2200 revolutions per minute drives through a gear ratio of 6. Calculate the speed of the output shaft in revolutions per minute.
items.s: Output speed = engine speed/gear ratio = 2200/6 = 366.7 revolutions per minute.

items.q: A gearbox receives 240 N m of torque from the engine and has a reduction ratio of 3. Calculate the torque at the output shaft in N m, taking the drive as ideal.
items.s: Output torque = input torque x gear ratio = 240 x 3 = 720 N m.

items.q: A pulley of 30 cm diameter running at 900 revolutions per minute drives a pulley of 75 cm diameter by a belt. Calculate the speed of the driven pulley.
items.s: N2 = N1 x D1/D2 = 900 x 30/75 = 360 revolutions per minute.

items.q: A belt runs on a pulley of 0.5 m diameter turning at 1000 revolutions per minute. Calculate the linear speed of the belt in m/s.
items.s: Belt speed = pi x diameter x speed/60 = pi x 0.5 x 1000/60 = 26.18 m/s.

items.q: The unit draft of a tillage implement is 8 kN per metre of width and the implement is 1.8 m wide. Calculate the total draft in kN.
items.s: Total draft = unit draft x width = 8 x 1.8 = 14.4 kN.

items.q: A plough requires a draft of 24 kN and is worked at 7 km/h. Calculate the power required to pull it in kW.
items.s: Draft power = draft x speed/3.6 = 24 x 7/3.6 = 46.67 kW.

items.q: An implement 2 m wide is worked at a speed of 9 km/h. Calculate the theoretical field capacity in hectares per hour.
items.s: Theoretical field capacity = width x speed/10 = 2 x 9/10 = 1.8 ha/h.

items.q: A machine of width 2 m works at 5 km/h and its field efficiency is 80 percent. Calculate the effective field capacity in hectares per hour.
items.s: Theoretical capacity = 2 x 5/10 = 1 ha/h, so effective capacity = 1 x 80/100 = 0.8 ha/h.

items.q: The theoretical field capacity of a machine is 3.6 ha/h while its effective field capacity is 1.5 ha/h. Calculate the field efficiency in percent.
items.s: Field efficiency = effective/theoretical x 100 = 1.5/3.6 x 100 = 41.7 percent.

items.q: A field of 12 hectares is to be worked by a machine whose effective field capacity is 2.4 ha/h. Calculate the time needed in hours.
items.s: Time = area/capacity = 12/2.4 = 5 hours.

items.q: A machine has an effective field capacity of 1.5 ha/h and works 9 hours in a day. Calculate the area it can cover in a day in hectares.
items.s: Area per day = capacity x hours = 1.5 x 9 = 13.5 hectares.

items.q: A tractor uses 18 litres of diesel per hour and works at an effective field capacity of 0.8 ha/h. Calculate the fuel consumption per hectare in litres.
items.s: Fuel per hectare = use per hour/capacity = 18/0.8 = 22.5 litres per hectare.

items.q: A crop is planted at a within row spacing of 30 cm with a row spacing of 50 cm. Calculate the plant population in plants per hectare.
items.s: Population = 100000000/(spacing x row spacing) = 100000000/(30 x 50) = 66667 plants per hectare.

items.q: A planter drops 45 seeds over a travelled distance of 1.5 m. Calculate the average number of seeds per metre of row.
items.s: Seeds per metre = number of seeds/distance = 45/1.5 = 30.

items.q: A combine harvester leaves 60 kg of grain per hectare on the ground while the total yield of the field is 3000 kg per hectare. Calculate the header loss in percent.
items.s: Header loss = grain lost/yield x 100 = 60/3000 x 100 = 2 percent.

items.q: A threshing machine handles 54 tonnes of crop in 4 hours. Calculate its throughput in tonnes per hour.
items.s: Throughput = mass/time = 54/4 = 13.5 tonnes per hour.

items.q: The cleaning unit of a thresher passes 1080 kg of clean grain out of a total output of 1200 kg of material. Calculate the cleaning efficiency in percent.
items.s: Cleaning efficiency = clean grain/total output x 100 = 1080/1200 x 100 = 90 percent.

items.q: A tractor costs 4500000 naira and is expected to have a salvage value of 600000 naira after 12 years. Calculate its annual depreciation by the straight line method in naira.
items.s: Depreciation = (cost - salvage value)/life = (4500000 - 600000)/12 = 325000 naira per year.

items.q: The annual fixed cost of a machine is 240000 naira, it is used for 800 hours in the year and its variable cost is 750 naira per hour. Calculate the total cost per hour in naira.
items.s: Fixed cost per hour = 240000/800 = 300 naira, so total cost per hour = 300 + 750 = 1050 naira.

items.q: An operation costs 1500 naira per hour and the machine works at an effective field capacity of 1 ha/h. Calculate the cost of the operation per hectare in naira.
items.s: Cost per hectare = cost per hour/capacity = 1500/1 = 1500 naira.

items.q: A pump of 3.5 kW runs for 6 hours and electrical energy costs 35 naira per kWh. Calculate the cost of the energy used in naira.
items.s: Energy used = 3.5 x 6 = 21 kWh, so cost = 21 x 35 = 735 naira.

items.q: A four stroke engine of 2.5 litre displacement develops 75 kW at 2200 revolutions per minute. Calculate the brake mean effective pressure in kPa.
items.s: bmep = 120000 x power/(displacement x speed) = 120000 x 75/(2.5 x 2200) = 1636 kPa.

items.q: An implement of width 3 m working at a depth of 0.3 m requires a draft of 12000 N. Calculate the specific draft in kPa.
items.s: Area of soil cut = 3 x 0.3 = 0.9 m2, so specific draft = 12000/0.9 = 13333 Pa = 13.33 kPa.

items.q: A machine costs 4000000 naira, will be worth 600000 naira at the end of its life, and the rate of interest on capital is 8 percent. Calculate the average annual interest charge in naira.
items.s: Average investment = (4000000 + 600000)/2 = 2300000, so interest = 2300000 x 8/100 = 184000 naira per year.

items.q: A pump delivers 12 litres per second against a total head of 30 m with an efficiency of 55 percent. Calculate the power required to drive it in kW.
items.s: Power = 9.81 x discharge x head/(1000 x efficiency) = 9.81 x 12 x 30/(1000 x 0.55) = 6.42 kW.

items.q: A tractor engine cylinder has a bore of 80 mm and a piston stroke of 130 mm. Calculate the swept volume of one cylinder in cm3.
items.s: Swept volume = (pi/4) x bore^2 x stroke = (pi/4) x 8^2 x 13 = 653.5 cm3.

items.q: A 3 cylinder four stroke engine has a bore of 90 mm and a stroke of 110 mm. Calculate its total piston displacement in litres.
items.s: One cylinder displaces 699.8 cm3, so 3 cylinders displace 3 x 699.8 = 2099 cm3 = 2.1 litres.

items.q: An engine develops a brake power of 35 kW at 2200 revolutions per minute. Calculate the torque it delivers in N m.
items.s: Torque = power x 60000/(2 x pi x speed) = 35 x 60000/(2 x pi x 2200) = 151.9 N m.

items.q: An engine uses 4.5 kg of fuel per hour, the fuel having a calorific value of 44 MJ/kg, and delivers 45 kW at the shaft. Calculate its brake thermal efficiency in percent.
items.s: Fuel power = 4.5 x 44/3.6 = 55 kW. Thermal efficiency = 45/55 x 100 = 81.8 percent.

items.q: A tractor engine consumes 9 kg of diesel per hour while delivering 40 kW at the shaft. Calculate the specific fuel consumption in kg/kWh.
items.s: Specific fuel consumption = fuel used per hour/power = 9/40 = 0.225 kg/kWh.

items.q: An engine burns 9.5 kg of fuel per hour and the calorific value of the fuel is 44.5 MJ/kg. Calculate the heat energy released per hour expressed as a power in kW.
items.s: Fuel power = mass per hour x calorific value/3.6 = 9.5 x 44.5/3.6 = 117.4 kW.

items.q: An engine takes in 660 kg of air per hour and burns 65 kg of fuel in the same period. Calculate the air fuel ratio.
items.s: Air fuel ratio = mass of air/mass of fuel = 660/65 = 10.2.

items.q: A tractor pulls an implement with a draft of 6 kN at a forward speed of 6 km/h. Calculate the drawbar power in kW.
items.s: Drawbar power = draft x speed/3.6 = 6 x 6/3.6 = 10 kW.

items.q: A tractor wheel would cover 250 m in a given time if it rolled without slipping but it actually covers 226 m. Calculate the wheel slip in percent.
items.s: Slip = (theoretical distance - actual distance)/theoretical distance x 100 = (250 - 226)/250 x 100 = 9.6 percent.

items.q: At a given setting a tractor delivers 22 kW at the drawbar while 25 kW reaches the driving wheels. Calculate the tractive efficiency in percent.
items.s: Tractive efficiency = drawbar power/wheel power x 100 = 22/25 x 100 = 88 percent.

items.q: A trailer of weight 25 kN runs on a soil whose coefficient of rolling resistance is 0.04. Calculate the rolling resistance in kN.
items.s: Rolling resistance = coefficient x weight = 0.04 x 25 = 1 kN.

items.q: The torque at the axle of a tractor wheel is 3000 N m and the rolling radius of the wheel is 0.7 m. Calculate the tractive force at the rim in N.
items.s: Tractive force = torque/radius = 3000/0.7 = 4286 N.

items.q: A drawbar pull of 7.5 kN must be developed on a soil where the coefficient of traction is 0.55. Calculate the vertical load needed on the driving wheels in kN.
items.s: Vertical load = pull/coefficient of traction = 7.5/0.55 = 13.64 kN.

items.q: An engine turning at 1600 revolutions per minute drives through a gear ratio of 3.5. Calculate the speed of the output shaft in revolutions per minute.
items.s: Output speed = engine speed/gear ratio = 1600/3.5 = 457.1 revolutions per minute.

items.q: A gearbox receives 120 N m of torque from the engine and has a reduction ratio of 4. Calculate the torque at the output shaft in N m, taking the drive as ideal.
items.s: Output torque = input torque x gear ratio = 120 x 4 = 480 N m.

items.q: A pulley of 25 cm diameter running at 1500 revolutions per minute drives a pulley of 45 cm diameter by a belt. Calculate the speed of the driven pulley.
items.s: N2 = N1 x D1/D2 = 1500 x 25/45 = 833.3 revolutions per minute.

items.q: A belt runs on a pulley of 0.3 m diameter turning at 1200 revolutions per minute. Calculate the linear speed of the belt in m/s.
items.s: Belt speed = pi x diameter x speed/60 = pi x 0.3 x 1200/60 = 18.85 m/s.

items.q: A plough requires a draft of 15 kN and is worked at 7 km/h. Calculate the power required to pull it in kW.
items.s: Draft power = draft x speed/3.6 = 15 x 7/3.6 = 29.17 kW.

items.q: An implement 2 m wide is worked at a speed of 6 km/h. Calculate the theoretical field capacity in hectares per hour.
items.s: Theoretical field capacity = width x speed/10 = 2 x 6/10 = 1.2 ha/h.

items.q: A machine of width 3.5 m works at 7 km/h and its field efficiency is 85 percent. Calculate the effective field capacity in hectares per hour.
items.s: Theoretical capacity = 3.5 x 7/10 = 2.45 ha/h, so effective capacity = 2.45 x 85/100 = 2.08 ha/h.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the mass of fuel burned for each unit of work delivered at the shaft”
o: mechanical efficiency
specific fuel consumption
volumetric efficiency
detonation
items.s: specific fuel consumption is the mass of fuel burned for each unit of work delivered at the shaft.

items.q: In this course, compression ratio refers to
o: the ratio of the total cylinder volume to the volume left above the piston at top dead centre
a cycle in which every turn of the crankshaft produces one power stroke
the highest position reached by the piston inside the cylinder
a nozzle that sprays metered fuel into the combustion chamber under high pressure
items.s: compression ratio: the ratio of the total cylinder volume to the volume left above the piston at top dead centre. The other options describe fuel injector, two stroke cycle, top dead centre.

items.q: “the rate at which the rotating drum of a thresher turns” is the definition of
o: throughput
cylinder speed
header loss
combine harvester
items.s: cylinder speed is the rate at which the rotating drum of a thresher turns.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a lump of soil left unbroken after a tillage operation”
o: specific draft
clod
harrow
subsoiler
items.s: clod is a lump of soil left unbroken after a tillage operation.

items.q: Three of these relate to Machinery costs and selection. Which one does not?
o: depreciation
draft
variable cost
fixed cost
items.s: Every other option belongs to Machinery costs and selection. “draft” belongs to Tillage tools and draft, not Machinery costs and selection.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the ratio of the horizontal pull developed to the vertical load carried by the driving wheels”
o: ballasting
drawbar power
coefficient of traction
tractive efficiency
items.s: coefficient of traction is the ratio of the horizontal pull developed to the vertical load carried by the driving wheels.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains mouldboard plough.
o: the pull required for each unit of cross sectional area of soil cut
an implement that cuts, lifts and turns a furrow slice over
the horizontal force needed to pull an implement through the soil
a machine whose powered blades chop and mix the soil in a single pass
items.s: mouldboard plough: an implement that cuts, lifts and turns a furrow slice over. The other options describe rotavator, draft, specific draft.

items.q: useful life may be defined as
o: the total cost of an operation divided by the area it covered
the price a machine is expected to fetch when it is finally sold
an expense that rises with the amount of work the machine does
the number of years a machine is expected to serve before replacement
items.s: useful life: the number of years a machine is expected to serve before replacement. The other options describe salvage value, variable cost, cost per hectare.

items.q: “a coupling that connects or disconnects the engine from the transmission” is the definition of
o: belt drive
differential
final drive
clutch
items.s: clutch is a coupling that connects or disconnects the engine from the transmission.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a nozzle that sprays metered fuel into the combustion chamber under high pressure”
o: valve clearance
governor
fuel injector
swept volume
items.s: fuel injector is a nozzle that sprays metered fuel into the combustion chamber under high pressure.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains fuel injector.
o: a cycle in which every turn of the crankshaft produces one power stroke
the small gap left between the valve stem and the rocker so that the valve can close fully when hot
a nozzle that sprays metered fuel into the combustion chamber under high pressure
the volume displaced by the piston as it travels from the top to the bottom of its stroke
items.s: fuel injector: a nozzle that sprays metered fuel into the combustion chamber under high pressure. The other options describe valve clearance, swept volume, two stroke cycle.

items.q: In this course, power take off refers to
o: the transmission of power between two pulleys by an endless flexible band
the turning effect of a force about the axis of a shaft
a coupling that connects or disconnects the engine from the transmission
the shaft at the rear of a tractor that drives machines mounted on or trailed by it
items.s: power take off: the shaft at the rear of a tractor that drives machines mounted on or trailed by it. The other options describe clutch, torque, belt drive.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains harrow.
o: the horizontal force needed to pull an implement through the soil
an implement with many tines or discs used to break clods and level a seedbed
an implement whose revolving concave discs cut and invert the soil
a heavy tined implement that loosens soil below the depth reached by ordinary ploughing
items.s: harrow: an implement with many tines or discs used to break clods and level a seedbed. The other options describe subsoiler, disc plough, draft.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines thermal efficiency?
o: the share of the heat energy in the fuel that is turned into useful work at the shaft
the ratio of the power delivered at the shaft to the power developed inside the cylinders
the explosive burning of the last part of the charge after the flame front has passed
a scale showing how readily a diesel fuel ignites when it is injected into hot air
items.s: thermal efficiency: the share of the heat energy in the fuel that is turned into useful work at the shaft. The other options describe cetane rating, detonation, mechanical efficiency.

items.q: “an implement that cuts, lifts and turns a furrow slice over” is the definition of
o: draft
harrow
specific draft
mouldboard plough
items.s: mouldboard plough is an implement that cuts, lifts and turns a furrow slice over.

items.q: The correct meaning of salvage value is
o: the number of years a machine is expected to serve before replacement
an expense that is incurred whether the machine works or not
the price a machine is expected to fetch when it is finally sold
the total cost of an operation divided by the area it covered
items.s: salvage value: the price a machine is expected to fetch when it is finally sold. The other options describe fixed cost, cost per hectare, useful life.

items.q: “the placing of single seeds at accurately spaced intervals along the row” is the definition of
o: metering mechanism
row spacing
thousand grain weight
precision planting
items.s: precision planting is the placing of single seeds at accurately spaced intervals along the row.

items.q: The correct meaning of harrow is
o: a lump of soil left unbroken after a tillage operation
an implement that cuts, lifts and turns a furrow slice over
the pull required for each unit of cross sectional area of soil cut
an implement with many tines or discs used to break clods and level a seedbed
items.s: harrow: an implement with many tines or discs used to break clods and level a seedbed. The other options describe mouldboard plough, clod, specific draft.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines differential lock?
o: the force that opposes the motion of a wheel over ground because the soil is pressed down
the ratio of the horizontal pull developed to the vertical load carried by the driving wheels
a control that makes both driving wheels turn together when one of them loses grip
the ratio of the power at the drawbar to the power delivered to the driving wheels
items.s: differential lock: a control that makes both driving wheels turn together when one of them loses grip. The other options describe rolling resistance, coefficient of traction, tractive efficiency.

items.q: In this course, final drive refers to
o: the number of turns of the driving gear needed to produce one turn of the driven gear
the transmission of power between two sprockets by a linked metal chain
the turning effect of a force about the axis of a shaft
the last reduction gear set that carries drive from the transmission to the wheels
items.s: final drive: the last reduction gear set that carries drive from the transmission to the wheels. The other options describe chain drive, gear ratio, torque.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines chain drive?
o: the turning effect of a force about the axis of a shaft
the transmission of power between two pulleys by an endless flexible band
the transmission of power between two sprockets by a linked metal chain
the last reduction gear set that carries drive from the transmission to the wheels
items.s: chain drive: the transmission of power between two sprockets by a linked metal chain. The other options describe torque, final drive, belt drive.

items.q: The correct meaning of differential lock is
o: the addition of weight to a tractor so that its driving wheels grip better
the power measured at the hitch where an implement is pulled
a control that makes both driving wheels turn together when one of them loses grip
the difference between the distance a driving wheel would travel unloaded and the distance it actually covers
items.s: differential lock: a control that makes both driving wheels turn together when one of them loses grip. The other options describe wheel slip, ballasting, drawbar power.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a machine whose powered blades chop and mix the soil in a single pass”
o: rotavator
subsoiler
disc plough
mouldboard plough
items.s: rotavator is a machine whose powered blades chop and mix the soil in a single pass.

items.q: theoretical field capacity may be defined as
o: the operation in a sequence that limits the output of the whole system
the area or mass of material handled by a machine in unit time
the area a machine would cover in unit time at full width and full speed without any stop
the working breadth of a machine measured at right angles to its direction of travel
items.s: theoretical field capacity: the area a machine would cover in unit time at full width and full speed without any stop. The other options describe work rate, implement width, bottleneck.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains salvage value.
o: the total cost of an operation divided by the area it covered
the price a machine is expected to fetch when it is finally sold
the letting out of a machine and its operator to another farmer for a fee
an expense that is incurred whether the machine works or not
items.s: salvage value: the price a machine is expected to fetch when it is finally sold. The other options describe fixed cost, custom hire, cost per hectare.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains turn around time.
o: the area or mass of material handled by a machine in unit time
the time lost at the end of a run in turning and lining up for the next run
the working breadth of a machine measured at right angles to its direction of travel
the area a machine would cover in unit time at full width and full speed without any stop
items.s: turn around time: the time lost at the end of a run in turning and lining up for the next run. The other options describe implement width, theoretical field capacity, work rate.

items.q: The correct meaning of drawbar power is
o: the power measured at the hitch where an implement is pulled
a control that makes both driving wheels turn together when one of them loses grip
the difference between the distance a driving wheel would travel unloaded and the distance it actually covers
the shift of load from the front axle to the rear axle caused by the pull of an implement
items.s: drawbar power: the power measured at the hitch where an implement is pulled. The other options describe wheel slip, weight transfer, differential lock.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains timeliness.
o: the ratio of the area actually covered to the area that could be covered in the same time
the ability to carry out a farm operation within the period when it gives the best return
the working breadth of a machine measured at right angles to its direction of travel
the time lost at the end of a run in turning and lining up for the next run
items.s: timeliness: the ability to carry out a farm operation within the period when it gives the best return. The other options describe turn around time, implement width, field efficiency.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains volumetric efficiency.
o: a scale showing how well a petrol resists knocking in a spark ignition engine
a scale showing how readily a diesel fuel ignites when it is injected into hot air
the ratio of the volume of air actually drawn in to the swept volume of the cylinders
the mass of air supplied for each unit mass of fuel burned
items.s: volumetric efficiency: the ratio of the volume of air actually drawn in to the swept volume of the cylinders. The other options describe cetane rating, octane rating, air fuel ratio.

items.q: “the number of years a machine is expected to serve before replacement” is the definition of
o: depreciation
custom hire
useful life
interest on investment
items.s: useful life is the number of years a machine is expected to serve before replacement.

items.q: Three of these relate to Engine principles and power. Which one does not?
o: four stroke cycle
two stroke cycle
power take off
compression ratio
items.s: Every other option belongs to Engine principles and power. “power take off” belongs to Power transmission and gearing, not Engine principles and power.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a scale showing how well a petrol resists knocking in a spark ignition engine”
o: octane rating
volumetric efficiency
calorific value
specific fuel consumption
items.s: octane rating is a scale showing how well a petrol resists knocking in a spark ignition engine.

items.q: two stroke cycle may be defined as
o: the volume displaced by the piston as it travels from the top to the bottom of its stroke
the ratio of the total cylinder volume to the volume left above the piston at top dead centre
the space left above the piston when it stands at the top of its travel
a cycle in which every turn of the crankshaft produces one power stroke
items.s: two stroke cycle: a cycle in which every turn of the crankshaft produces one power stroke. The other options describe compression ratio, swept volume, clearance volume.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an implement with many tines or discs used to break clods and level a seedbed”
o: subsoiler
harrow
draft
mouldboard plough
items.s: harrow is an implement with many tines or discs used to break clods and level a seedbed.

items.q: The correct meaning of wheel slip is
o: the addition of weight to a tractor so that its driving wheels grip better
the shift of load from the front axle to the rear axle caused by the pull of an implement
the mounting that carries an implement behind a tractor and controls the depth of work
the difference between the distance a driving wheel would travel unloaded and the distance it actually covers
items.s: wheel slip: the difference between the distance a driving wheel would travel unloaded and the distance it actually covers. The other options describe ballasting, weight transfer, three point linkage.

items.q: fuel injector may be defined as
o: a nozzle that sprays metered fuel into the combustion chamber under high pressure
a device that mixes petrol with air before the mixture is drawn into the engine
a mechanism that holds engine speed steady by varying the fuel supplied as the load changes
the highest position reached by the piston inside the cylinder
items.s: fuel injector: a nozzle that sprays metered fuel into the combustion chamber under high pressure. The other options describe carburettor, governor, top dead centre.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains threshing.
o: the sieves and blower that remove chaff and broken material from threshed grain
the rate at which the rotating drum of a thresher turns
the separation of grain from the ear or pod by impact, rubbing or beating
the mass of crop a machine handles in unit time
items.s: threshing: the separation of grain from the ear or pod by impact, rubbing or beating. The other options describe cylinder speed, cleaning shoe, throughput.

items.q: “a one way valve at the foot of a suction pipe that keeps the pump primed” is the definition of
o: foot valve
cavitation
total head
suction lift
items.s: foot valve is a one way valve at the foot of a suction pipe that keeps the pump primed.

items.q: unit draft may be defined as
o: an implement that cuts, lifts and turns a furrow slice over
the pull required for each unit of cross sectional area of soil cut
the horizontal force needed to pull an implement through the soil
the pull required for each unit width of an implement
items.s: unit draft: the pull required for each unit width of an implement. The other options describe draft, mouldboard plough, specific draft.

items.q: The correct meaning of chain drive is
o: the gear arrangement that lets the two driving wheels turn at different speeds on a curve
the shaft at the rear of a tractor that drives machines mounted on or trailed by it
the number of turns of the driving gear needed to produce one turn of the driven gear
the transmission of power between two sprockets by a linked metal chain
items.s: chain drive: the transmission of power between two sprockets by a linked metal chain. The other options describe power take off, differential, gear ratio.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines useful life?
o: the fall in the value of a machine through age, wear and obsolescence
the price a machine is expected to fetch when it is finally sold
an expense that is incurred whether the machine works or not
the number of years a machine is expected to serve before replacement
items.s: useful life: the number of years a machine is expected to serve before replacement. The other options describe salvage value, fixed cost, depreciation.

items.q: threshing efficiency may be defined as
o: the separation of grain from the ear or pod by impact, rubbing or beating
the unthreshed heads and partly cleaned grain returned for a second pass
the proportion of the grain in the crop that is separated from the straw
a machine that cuts, threshes and cleans a grain crop in one operation
items.s: threshing efficiency: the proportion of the grain in the crop that is separated from the straw. The other options describe tailings, combine harvester, threshing.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines seed rate?
o: the mass or number of seeds sown on a unit area of land
the distance between the centres of two adjacent crop rows
the proportion of seeds that produce normal seedlings under test conditions
the part of a seeder that measures out seed at a steady rate
items.s: seed rate: the mass or number of seeds sown on a unit area of land. The other options describe germination percentage, metering mechanism, row spacing.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains cost per hectare.
o: the charge for the capital tied up in a machine
the total cost of an operation divided by the area it covered
the price a machine is expected to fetch when it is finally sold
the number of years a machine is expected to serve before replacement
items.s: cost per hectare: the total cost of an operation divided by the area it covered. The other options describe interest on investment, useful life, salvage value.

items.q: In this course, fuel injector refers to
o: a nozzle that sprays metered fuel into the combustion chamber under high pressure
the highest position reached by the piston inside the cylinder
the ratio of the total cylinder volume to the volume left above the piston at top dead centre
a cycle in which every turn of the crankshaft produces one power stroke
items.s: fuel injector: a nozzle that sprays metered fuel into the combustion chamber under high pressure. The other options describe top dead centre, two stroke cycle, compression ratio.

items.q: The correct meaning of metering mechanism is
o: the mass or number of seeds sown on a unit area of land
the number of plants standing on a unit area of land
the part of a seeder that measures out seed at a steady rate
the placing of single seeds at accurately spaced intervals along the row
items.s: metering mechanism: the part of a seeder that measures out seed at a steady rate. The other options describe plant population, precision planting, seed rate.

items.q: The correct meaning of power take off is
o: the number of turns of the driving gear needed to produce one turn of the driven gear
the shaft at the rear of a tractor that drives machines mounted on or trailed by it
the turning effect of a force about the axis of a shaft
the gear arrangement that lets the two driving wheels turn at different speeds on a curve
items.s: power take off: the shaft at the rear of a tractor that drives machines mounted on or trailed by it. The other options describe differential, torque, gear ratio.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains cylinder speed.
o: the rate at which the rotating drum of a thresher turns
the grain left on the ground or on the stubble by the cutting unit of a harvester
the unthreshed heads and partly cleaned grain returned for a second pass
the sieves and blower that remove chaff and broken material from threshed grain
items.s: cylinder speed: the rate at which the rotating drum of a thresher turns. The other options describe header loss, cleaning shoe, tailings.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the pressure surge caused by a sudden stop in the flow of water in a pipe”
o: suction lift
water hammer
pump efficiency
foot valve
items.s: water hammer is the pressure surge caused by a sudden stop in the flow of water in a pipe.

items.q: “the ratio of the power delivered at the shaft to the power developed inside the cylinders” is the definition of
o: brake power
air fuel ratio
calorific value
mechanical efficiency
items.s: mechanical efficiency is the ratio of the power delivered at the shaft to the power developed inside the cylinders.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines unit draft?
o: an implement whose revolving concave discs cut and invert the soil
an implement that cuts, lifts and turns a furrow slice over
a lump of soil left unbroken after a tillage operation
the pull required for each unit width of an implement
items.s: unit draft: the pull required for each unit width of an implement. The other options describe disc plough, clod, mouldboard plough.

items.q: In this course, chain drive refers to
o: the transmission of power between two pulleys by an endless flexible band
a coupling that connects or disconnects the engine from the transmission
the turning effect of a force about the axis of a shaft
the transmission of power between two sprockets by a linked metal chain
items.s: chain drive: the transmission of power between two sprockets by a linked metal chain. The other options describe belt drive, torque, clutch.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines effective field capacity?
o: the area actually covered in unit time after allowing for turns, refilling and other delays
the area a machine would cover in unit time at full width and full speed without any stop
the ratio of the area actually covered to the area that could be covered in the same time
the working breadth of a machine measured at right angles to its direction of travel
items.s: effective field capacity: the area actually covered in unit time after allowing for turns, refilling and other delays. The other options describe field efficiency, implement width, theoretical field capacity.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains effective field capacity.
o: the ability to carry out a farm operation within the period when it gives the best return
the area actually covered in unit time after allowing for turns, refilling and other delays
the operation in a sequence that limits the output of the whole system
the area a machine would cover in unit time at full width and full speed without any stop
items.s: effective field capacity: the area actually covered in unit time after allowing for turns, refilling and other delays. The other options describe timeliness, bottleneck, theoretical field capacity.

items.q: The correct meaning of weight transfer is
o: the ratio of the power at the drawbar to the power delivered to the driving wheels
the shift of load from the front axle to the rear axle caused by the pull of an implement
the addition of weight to a tractor so that its driving wheels grip better
the difference between the distance a driving wheel would travel unloaded and the distance it actually covers
items.s: weight transfer: the shift of load from the front axle to the rear axle caused by the pull of an implement. The other options describe tractive efficiency, wheel slip, ballasting.

items.q: The correct meaning of combine harvester is
o: the gap between the threshing drum and the curved grate beneath it
the grain left on the ground or on the stubble by the cutting unit of a harvester
the sieves and blower that remove chaff and broken material from threshed grain
a machine that cuts, threshes and cleans a grain crop in one operation
items.s: combine harvester: a machine that cuts, threshes and cleans a grain crop in one operation. The other options describe cleaning shoe, concave clearance, header loss.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains four stroke cycle.
o: the small gap left between the valve stem and the rocker so that the valve can close fully when hot
a device that mixes petrol with air before the mixture is drawn into the engine
the sequence of intake, compression, power and exhaust strokes completed in two turns of the crankshaft
the space left above the piston when it stands at the top of its travel
items.s: four stroke cycle: the sequence of intake, compression, power and exhaust strokes completed in two turns of the crankshaft. The other options describe clearance volume, carburettor, valve clearance.

items.q: The correct meaning of planter is
o: the distance between the centres of two adjacent crop rows
the mass or number of seeds sown on a unit area of land
the part of a seeder that measures out seed at a steady rate
a machine that places individual seeds or vegetative material at a set spacing
items.s: planter: a machine that places individual seeds or vegetative material at a set spacing. The other options describe seed rate, row spacing, metering mechanism.

items.q: “the last reduction gear set that carries drive from the transmission to the wheels” is the definition of
o: differential
torque
clutch
final drive
items.s: final drive is the last reduction gear set that carries drive from the transmission to the wheels.

the useful power measured at the output shaft of an engine
the ratio of the volume of air actually drawn in to the swept volume of the cylinders
the explosive burning of the last part of the charge after the flame front has passed
items.s: volumetric efficiency: the ratio of the volume of air actually drawn in to the swept volume of the cylinders. The other options describe detonation, cetane rating, brake power.

fixed cost
useful life
items.s: useful life is the number of years a machine is expected to serve before replacement.

the explosive burning of the last part of the charge after the flame front has passed
the mass of fuel burned for each unit of work delivered at the shaft
a scale showing how readily a diesel fuel ignites when it is injected into hot air

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains detonation.
o: a scale showing how well a petrol resists knocking in a spark ignition engine
the heat released when unit mass of a fuel is burned completely
the explosive burning of the last part of the charge after the flame front has passed
the mass of fuel burned for each unit of work delivered at the shaft
items.s: detonation: the explosive burning of the last part of the charge after the flame front has passed. The other options describe calorific value, octane rating, specific fuel consumption.

the gap between the threshing drum and the curved grate beneath it
a machine that cuts, threshes and cleans a grain crop in one operation
the separation of grain from the ear or pod by impact, rubbing or beating
items.s: threshing: the separation of grain from the ear or pod by impact, rubbing or beating. The other options describe concave clearance, combine harvester, tailings.

items.q: In this course, wheel slip refers to
o: a control that makes both driving wheels turn together when one of them loses grip
the shift of load from the front axle to the rear axle caused by the pull of an implement
the difference between the distance a driving wheel would travel unloaded and the distance it actually covers
the ratio of the power at the drawbar to the power delivered to the driving wheels
items.s: wheel slip: the difference between the distance a driving wheel would travel unloaded and the distance it actually covers. The other options describe tractive efficiency, weight transfer, differential lock.
